subject: Northbound eval: traffic intake & success milestones
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Bethany Liu <bethany@northbound.health>, James Lewis <james.lewis@northbound.health>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Northbound eval: traffic intake & success milestones

Hi Bethany / James —

Thanks again for the demo call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can lock the trial window and success guardrails. I've called out owners below.

Recap (what we heard)
- Evaluation goal: validate Redwood Dedicated can meet Northbound's production latency and cost targets for the conversational assistant and nightly batch enrichment job.
- Workloads: interactive chat (user-facing API) + periodic enrichment pipelines that trigger short high-throughput bursts.

Needed from Northbound (James / Bethany) — traffic intake items
- Typical steady-state RPS (avg) and typical concurrency per region (US/EU)
- Burst profile: peak RPS, typical burst duration, frequency (e.g., 5x for 20–40s every evening)
- Token lengths: median/95th for user messages and model responses (sample or percentile helps)
- Example request/response sizes and any streaming vs. non-streaming patterns
- Any IP/firewall requirements for trial endpoints and team ACLs

Example acceptance criteria (Redwood proposal)
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency < 250 ms for 1–2 token steps (short chitchat) and < 600 ms for 120-token outputs under target concurrency.
- Errors: <2% client-visible error rate during the 72-hr soak at expected concurrency.
- Cost: cost per 1k tokens should not exceed the projected threshold we discussed (we'll compute once we have token mix).
- Functional: model outputs pass your 5 sample prompts (you’ll provide golden prompts later).

Proposed evaluation plan & timeline
- Week 0 (this week): Receive traffic snapshot + confirm trial start date (owner: James) — items listed above.
- Week 1: Redwood provision Dedicated trial environment + preconfigured load harness (owner: Aditya).
- Week 2: Controlled load runs (daytime steady-state + scheduled bursts) + run your golden prompts and automated QA (owner: Aditya / Marissa).
- Acceptance window: 72-hr soak demonstrating SLOs above.

Ownership
- Northbound: James (DevOps) — provide traffic snapshot, open firewall, and schedule any network windows. Bethany — product/QA contact for golden prompt validation.
- Redwood: Olga (AE) — timeline & canary coordination; Aditya (Solutions Eng) — test harness, load runs; Marissa (CS) — onboarding/runbook.

Next steps (please reply with items you can attach or confirm)
1) James: attach the traffic export (CSV) with RPS by minute + token-length sample if available. [stub: northbound-traffic-snapshot.csv]
2) Bethany: confirm whether PII masking is required for test data or we should use synthetic datasets.
3) Redwood: we’ll send a Drive folder with the eval template and a HubSpot update for the deal (NB-4781).

If that all looks good I'll pencil in a start on Monday Dec 7 and block Aditya's calendar for provisioning and the initial load run.

Thanks —
Olga
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Northbound eval: traffic intake & success milestones

Hi Olga — thanks for the clear recap. We can provide the CSV and some percentile token samples; attaching the first pass.

Quick answers up front:
- Typical steady-state RPS (US primary region): avg 12 RPS across user-facing assistant, peaking to ~150 RPS during marketing-driven bursts (these last ~20–45s; happen ~2x/day).
- Concurrency: usually 18–28 concurrent sessions during steady hours; bursts push concurrent to ~220 for short windows.
- Token lengths: user messages median ~18 tokens, 95th ~72 tokens; model responses median ~110 tokens, 95th ~420 tokens.
- Enrichment pipelines: batch jobs run nightly at 02:00 local and cause short 5–7 minute spikes reaching ~500 RPS to our internal ingestion service (not user-facing).

Attachments: northbound-traffic-snapshot.csv (minute-level RPS for last 7 days), sample_request_examples.txt

PII: For the trial we prefer synthetic/scrubbed data. We will redact direct PII before uploading; we may ask you to confirm if masking is sufficient.

We'd prefer the trial start on Mon Dec 7 if that still works for your team.

—Bethany
Head of Product — Northbound Health
[attachment: northbound-traffic-snapshot.csv]
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Northbound eval: traffic intake & success milestones

Thanks Bethany — that snapshot is exactly what we needed. Key follow-ups for our side:

1) Aditya: can you size a Dedicated trial with a profile that covers both the 500 RPS 5–7 min batch spike and the 150 RPS short bursts while keeping steady-state cost sensible? Please include the KV cache and batching config we'd recommend. Deliverable: short sizing note + provisioning playbook by Wed Nov 2 (typo: Dec 2).

2) Marissa: prep the onboarding checklist and the golden prompt suite request (Bethany will share 5 canonical prompts for functional validation).

3) James / Northbound: please confirm firewall egress rules — we'll send IP ranges for the Dedicated trial cluster. Also confirm if synthetic data is OK (Bethany said yes; please confirm).

I'll create a shared Drive folder and update HubSpot with the trial timeline (NB-4781). Aditya / Marissa — I'll assign calendar blocks for Dec 7–11 for provisioning and tests.

Also noting region = US per their traffic; include extra headroom for the late-night enrichment spikes.

Olga
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Confirming we'll upload a redacted CSV to the Drive folder by EOD today and open the firewall window for test IPs. A couple clarifications from ops:
- The 500 RPS batch spike is internal-only but triggers additional downstream calls to the assistant for enrichment; we want Redwood to simulate that full pipeline (so please size for end-to-end peak).
- Concurrency during marketing bursts correlates with external referrer traffic; these are short and unpredictable — recommend two burst profiles in the harness (150 RPS x 30s, 220 RPS x 15s).
- We'll also provide a short list of user-agent headers and geo distribution (mostly us-east/us-west).

I'll post the upload link and firewall request in the shared Drive and ping infra once done.

James
DevOps Lead — Northbound Health
